Hi Liam — thanks for taking time today. Quick recap and a few items to help us align pricing/packaging ahead of procurement: 

Call recap (short):
- Primary use case: customer-facing summarization and search across support docs (ingestion + real-time inference).
- Expected steady-state traffic: ~1500 qps at peak hours (batching possible for lower-latency paths).
- Data residency: US-only, will need VPC options for production.

Key procurement / commercial questions we heard on the call:
1) Purchasing route: does legal/procurement require Purchase Order (PO) or can you pay on card? Any procurement portals or marketplace preference?
2) Commitment appetite: would you consider a 12-month commit for a dedicated pool in exchange for a discount vs on-demand hosted? If so, a rough committed spend range would help (bands are fine).
3) Security docs: you asked for SOC 2 and data retention terms — attaching our standard checklist and a short pricing summary to speed internal review.

Attachments: silverline-procurement-checklist.pdf, redwood-pricing-summary-2027Q1.xlsx (pricing bands & quick compare: hosted / dedicated / private).

Next steps I propose:
- Liam/Karen: confirm preferred purchasing mechanism (PO vs card vs marketplace) and whether procurement needs us in their vendor portal.
- If committed path is interesting, share a high-level committed spend band (e.g., $X–$Y / month) so we can model discount tiers and sizing for dedicated capacity.
- We'll pull in pricing options and a short one-page SOW stub if needed.

If helpful, I can set a 30-minute follow-up with our commerce ops (Ben) and engineering ops (Sergio) later this week.

Thanks —
Marissa Cole

Subject: Re: Commercial readiness & purchasing path — Silverline follow-up

Marissa — thanks for the recap. A few answers from procurement and ops: 

- Purchasing: Procurement strongly prefers PO (net 30) for any committed agreements. Cards ok for small POCs (< $5k).
- Marketplace: we have a company policy that prefers marketplace purchases when parity exists (for easier cataloguing), but procurement will accept direct vendor PO if the pricing or terms are materially better.
- Commitment: we are open to a 12-month committed arrangement if the discount is significant and we can lock a baseline capacity for peak months. For sizing: current estimate is $25k–$45k/mo in run-rate cloud spend for inference (this is an early ballpark).
- Security: SOC2 Type II and data residency controls are mandatory. We will circulate vendor questionnaire (I'll attach separately).

Karen is procurement lead — looping her for next steps. Can you confirm whether a dedicated pool (pinned GPUs) requires additional procurement approvals vs hosted reserved capacity? Also curious about whether Redwood can support a hybrid approach (hosted + private VPC for sensitive flows).

— Liam

Marissa / Sergio — thanks for the context. Actionable plan below and linked attachments.

Summary recommendation (short):
- Offer 3-tier pricing card for Silverline:
  * Band A (mid): $25k/mo committed (12m) — Hosted committed plan — ~15% discount vs on-demand; includes standard support; VPC add-on available.
  * Band B (mid-high): $35k/mo committed (12m) — Hosted committed plan — ~22% discount; includes higher throughput SLAs and priority scheduling on dedicated pools when available.
  * Band C (high): $45k/mo committed (12m) — Dedicated pool (reserved GPUs) — ~30% discount; includes capacity reservation, 2-week lead time for scaling, and enterprise support.

- PO vs card: We can accept PO for committed deals (legal will require signature on MSA + SOW, invoice net30). Card is fine for POCs <$5k as Liam noted. Marketplace purchase is supported but pricing parity must be verified — marketplace listing adds ~10% catalog fee on some clouds. Recommend direct PO for better economics; we can provide marketplace quoting if they insist.

- Hybrid approach: Supported. Recommend starting hosted committed to reduce ops lift, then transition sensitive flows to Private/VPC for regulated documents (Sergio, estimate lead time ~3–4 weeks to stand up VPC connectors once contract signed).

Attachments (for Silverline and internal review): rdw-hosted-vs-dedicated-quicknote.pdf, redwood-pricing-summary-2027Q1.xlsx (pricing bands).

Next steps:
1) Marissa: share the three-tier pricing summary with Liam/Karen and ask them to confirm preferred band or provide a narrower committed spend range.
2) I'll prepare a short MSA + SOW template with PO invoicing terms and send to legal for approval (target EOD Mon).
3) Sergio: can you confirm the 3–4 week lead time estimate and any blackout windows for Q2?

Happy to join a call with procurement if they want walk-through of invoicing and marketplace options.
